expectations.text: Every finding carries a severity grade and all findings appear in one strict total rank order
expectations.evidence: Every finding carries a severity grade (Critical C1-C3, High H1-H4, Medium M1-M4, Low L1-L2) and all 13 appear in one summary table ordered by tier. But the order is a tiered partial order, not a strict total rank: nothing states C1 outranks C2 or M1 outranks M4 -- within-tier numbering is enumeration, and no text claims a ranking. Findings within a tier are effectively tied.

expectations.text: Every finding includes a concrete failure scenario tied to downstream harm
expectations.evidence: C1-H4 each have an explicit 'What actually breaks' paragraph (e.g., C2: 'Krakow primary acks a 10:00 CET Sev1, hits a login wall on the prod bastion, and burns the 15-minute escalation window'). M/L findings state harm inline and in the summary table's 'What breaks' column (M3: 'an incident straddling 20:00 CET gets a fresh responder with zero state'; L1: 'every boundary is off by an hour all summer').

expectations.text: Report identifies the timezone coverage gap: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET, leaving 20:00-02:00 ET covered by neither window
expectations.evidence: C1: 'Krakow's 08:00-20:00 CET is 02:00-14:00 ET. US covers 08:00-20:00 ET. Combined coverage is 02:00-20:00 ET. Nothing covers 20:00-02:00 ET.' Arithmetic verified correct (ET/CET offset is 6 hours in both standard and daylight periods).

expectations.text: Report identifies Krakow readiness risk: 6-week-old team, no production experience, access provisioning incomplete before go-live
expectations.evidence: C2 stacks all three: 'Joined 6 weeks ago, never shipped to production', 'Prod SSH, dashboards, and PagerDuty access are "in progress" with no completion date or gate', 'One week of shadowing, then live in under a month.' Matches the plan's Notes section.

expectations.text: Report identifies that the US-only incident-commander pool still wakes US engineers, undermining the zero-overnight-pages metric
expectations.evidence: C3: 'the IC pool is entirely US-based... A Sev1 at 10:00 CET is 04:00 ET. So every serious incident in the Krakow shift pages a sleeping US engineer anyway. This contradicts the goal ("eliminate overnight pages for US-East")... it makes the success metric ("zero overnight pages") either false or... a perverse incentive.'

expectations.text: Report states plainly (in a verdict or top-ranked finding) that the plan fails its own stated goal as written, not merely a list of individual risks
expectations.evidence: Top finding C1: 'Follow-the-sun with two regions only 6 hours apart is arithmetically impossible with 12-hour shifts... The plan cannot deliver its title with the teams it has' and 'fails the plan's only success metric on day one'. Closing verdict: 'The plan's core arithmetic is broken: two regions 6 hours apart cannot follow the sun with 12-hour shifts.'

expectations.text: Coverage includes at least two of: cross-shift handover of in-flight incidents, weekend or US/Polish holiday misalignment, DST drift between US and EU changeover weeks, rollback/abort criteria
expectations.evidence: Three of four: M3 (handover: 'no rule for who owns an incident that is open at the boundary'), M4 (DST: 'The US and EU change clocks on different dates... the offset drops to 5 hours, growing the nightly hole to 7 hours'), M2 (rollback: 'no threshold ("if Krakow misses N pages... US resumes 24/7")'). Holiday misalignment is absent.

expectations.text: Retest mechanism is one falsifiable per-finding check, not verbatim scenario copies
expectations.evidence: No per-finding retest checks exist. A few findings embed fix gates (C2: live-fire drill; H3: 3-5 game-day scenarios), but there is no retest section and most findings (C1, C3, H1, H2, M1-M4, L1-L2) have no falsifiable check at all.

expectations.text: Report includes a bottom-line verdict plus a prioritized minimum-changes list
expectations.evidence: A bottom-line verdict exists ('The shape of the fix': core arithmetic broken, three honest options a/b/c). The closing 'gate go-live on:' list (verified prod access, game-day-tested runbooks, 4+ weeks shadow, in-region secondary, EU-timezone IC, outcome metrics, rollback criteria) is a minimum-changes list but carries no priority order -- items are comma-listed with no ranking or sequencing claim.

claims.claim: CET is 6 hours ahead of ET; Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET
claims.evidence: EST=UTC-5/CET=UTC+1 and EDT=UTC-4/CEST=UTC+2 both give a 6-hour offset; the conversion is correct.

claims.claim: US and EU change clocks on different dates, dropping the offset to 5 hours for roughly three weeks a year
claims.evidence: US changes mid-March/early November; EU late March/late October. During the mismatch the offset is 5 hours, as the report and user_notes state.

claims.claim: The IC pool is entirely US-based and stays as-is
claims.evidence: Plan item 5: 'the current IC pool is all US-based, which stays as-is for now.'

claims.claim: Krakow has 3 engineers, joined 6 weeks ago, has not shipped to production, access 'in progress', no headcount budget
claims.evidence: All match oncall-rotation-plan.md Goal and Notes sections verbatim.

claims.claim: Industry floor for a sustainable rotation is 4-6 people
claims.evidence: Common SRE guidance cites minimums in this range, but the report gives no source; treat as plausible but uncited.

uncertainties: Timezone arithmetic assumption (6-hour offset, 5 during DST mismatch) underpins C1 and M4 -- verified correct by grader

suggestions.expectation: Every finding carries a severity grade and all findings appear in one strict total rank order
suggestions.reason: This bundles two checks with different discrimination power. Severity grading is nearly free (any competent review does it); strict total ordering is the real skill discriminator. Splitting them would show partial credit honestly instead of failing the whole expectation on the ordering half.

suggestions.expectation: Report states plainly (in a verdict or top-ranked finding) that the plan fails its own stated goal as written
suggestions.reason: Passed here on genuine substance, but a review that merely echoes 'the plan has risks' in a summary paragraph could arguably scrape by. Consider requiring the verdict name the specific goal ('eliminate overnight pages') it fails.

eval_feedback.overall: The expectation set discriminates well for this baseline: the three failures (strict total rank order, per-finding retest checks, prioritized changes list) are exactly the structural artifacts a review skill would enforce, while the six passes reflect analysis quality any strong reviewer produces. No transcript was available, so process claims rest solely on user_notes.md and metrics.json.
